label: prf:plancherel-term-7-formulation
title: Proof of plancherel term 7 formulation
html:
Proof.

Each \{\lambda : \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) = k\} is finite, so each \Phi_k is a finite R-valued sum. By curvature-rank stratification, the central idempotent e_\lambda has GB-filtration depth \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) — assumed, not established; see the gap note below — so binning \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) \cdot \log|\int_{A_\lambda} \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K}) \cdot \mathcal{T}| by \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) is the canonical curvature-rank decomposition of the (logarithmic) Frobenius pairing. The threshold k \geq 4 is determined by which strata of Z(H_n(R, q)) still carry a distinguished knot ideal — empirically k_* = 4.

The total sum is bounded: \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} w_\lambda(q) is finite for every n and equals 1 exactly at q = 1; at q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps) it deviates from 1 — categorically \sum w_\lambda(q) \approx 1.51 at n = 12 (prop:plancherel-weight-boundedness remark on q-deformed alternative). Boundedness of \Phi_k follows from finiteness of the w_\lambda(q) together with finiteness of the per-block log-Frobenius pairings; the absolute-convergence constant is \sup_\lambda w_\lambda(q) \cdot \#\Lambda_k \cdot \sup_\lambda |\log|\!\int||, not 1 as for the classical Plancherel measure. \square

Logarithmic control of scale. The bare Wedderburn-weighted character sum \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) \cdot \chi_\lambda(\beta) / \dim_q V_\lambda is bounded by a finite constant (canonical \lesssim 2 at q_0 for n \leq 12), giving a similarly small MeV-scale ceiling — too small for MeV-scale binding gaps. Replacing \chi_\lambda with \log|\!\int_{A_\lambda}\!\cdot| keeps the Wedderburn weighting bounded but lets each block contribute O(\log|\chi|), which can be large. This is how the formula reaches \sim 30 MeV {}^4\mathrm{He} binding from a bounded measure: logarithmic unbounding of bounded characters.

Comparison with the deprecated bare hook product. An older form of "Term 7" used the Hopf hook polynomial H_q(\lambda) = \prod_{x \in \lambda}[h_x]_q summed naively across deep partitions; that form diverges as q^{n^2/2}. The Wedderburn- weighted log functional above is the categorically correct replacement — it descends from the Hochschild-cohomology spectral sequence's collapse at E_1 (spectral sequence collapse), with \mathrm{HH}^0 = Z(H_n(R, q)) paired against the logarithmic Frobenius integral.

Naming note. Earlier drafts (and the legacy formalism the formal derivation) referred to w_\lambda(q) = \dim_q^2/[n]_q! as the "q-Plancherel weight" and claimed \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) = 1 via a "q-Plancherel identity" \sum_\lambda \dim_q^2 V_\lambda = [n]_q!. That identity does not hold in H_n(R, q) at generic q — the Hecke algebra is a flat deformation with \dim_{\mathbb{Q}(q)} H_n = n! and Wedderburn–Artin gives the classical Plancherel identity \sum_\lambda (\dim V_\lambda)^2 = n!, whose Plancherel weight is w_\lambda(1) := (\dim V_\lambda)^2/n! (prop:plancherel-weight-boundedness). The current proposition uses w_\lambda(q) as the q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight, not the Plancherel measure; they coincide at q = 1.

canonical witness. the formal derivation computes \Phi_k for D, T, {}^3\mathrm{He}, {}^4\mathrm{He}, evaluating \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathrm{atom}) via Hoefsmit seminormal form characters at q_0 and summing with the q-deformed Wedderburn weights w_\lambda(q). Compares \alpha \cdot \mathfrak{m}^{\geq 4}_{q,\mathcal{K}} to the Coulomb-corrected nuclear binding B_\mathrm{nucl} from coulomb-subtracted-binding.witness.json.

Gap (2026-08-16). The step above reads a grading of the centre by partition depth off a proposition that stratifies H_n(R,q) by the curvature rank of words. That identification is not stated in the cited proposition, and the three readings of J^\bullet present in the corpus are each excluded: the ideal-power reading is provably \bot above degree 0 (QOU.BraidKnot.WordFiltration.map_pow_eq_bot); the Coxeter-length reading fails a dimension count at n \leq 3; and the rewrite-depth reading is identically zero once def:hecke-normal-form fixes T_w as the unique normal-form basis indexed by S_n. Analysis: docs/audits/2026-08-16-three-gb-filtrations-one-name.md. Not claimed: that this block's conclusion is false — only that the step it rests on is unestablished, and that the obvious ways to establish it do not work.
